title: UPSC Civil Services Exam (CSE) Guide: Complete IAS/IPS Roadmap
summary: Comprehensive preparation strategy for UPSC Civil Services Examination covering Prelims, Mains, Optional subjects, and Interview guidance.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction

The UPSC Civil Services Examination (CSE) conducted by the Union Public Service Commission is the gateway to India's premier administrative and diplomatic positions, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), and Indian Revenue Service (IRS). Known for its academic rigor and intellectual depth, cracking UPSC requires structured planning, extensive conceptual understanding, and consistent answer-writing practice over 10 to 12 months.

## Eligibility Criteria

| Parameter | Requirements |
|---|---|
| **Educational Qualification** | Bachelor's Degree in any discipline from a recognized University or deemed university. Candidates in their final year of graduation can apply for Prelims. |
| **Nationality** | Must be a citizen of India for IAS and IPS. For other services, candidates may be citizens of India, subjects of Nepal/Bhutan, or Tibetan refugees. |
| **Number of Attempts** | General: 6 attempts; OBC/EWS: 9 attempts; SC/ST: Unlimited attempts up to the upper age limit. |
| **Physical Fitness** | Physical & medical fitness verified by Central Standing Medical Board (CSMB). Special visual and height criteria apply for IPS/IRTS. |
| **Language Competence** | Candidates can write the Mains Examination in English, Hindi, or any language listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution. |

## Age Limit & Category Relaxation

| Category | Base Age Limit | Age Relaxation Years | Maximum Attempts |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General (UR)** | 21 - 32 Years | Nil (0 Years) | 6 Attempts |
| **Economically Weaker Section (EWS)** | 21 - 32 Years | Nil (0 Years) | 6 Attempts |
| **Other Backward Classes (OBC)** | 21 - 32 Years | Up to 3 Years | 9 Attempts |
| **Scheduled Castes (SC)** | 21 - 32 Years | Up to 5 Years | Unlimited Attempts |
| **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** | 21 - 32 Years | Up to 5 Years | Unlimited Attempts |
| **PwBD (General / OBC)** | 21 - 32 Years | Up to 10 Years | 9 Attempts |
| **PwBD (SC / ST)** | 21 - 32 Years | Up to 15 Years | Unlimited Attempts |
| **Ex-Servicemen (Commissioned)** | 21 - 32 Years | Up to 5 Years | As per relaxation |

## Examination Structure & Pattern

| Stage / Paper | Subject / Focus | Total Marks | Duration | Qualifying / Merit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Prelims Paper I** | General Studies (Polity, History, Economy, Geo, Env, Sci) | 200 Marks | 2 Hours | Merit for Mains Cut-off (1/3rd Negative Marking) |
| **Prelims Paper II (CSAT)** | Comprehension, Logical Reasoning & Basic Numeracy | 200 Marks | 2 Hours | Qualifying Only (Must score 33% / 66 marks) |
| **Mains Paper A** | Compulsory Indian Language (from 8th Schedule) | 300 Marks | 3 Hours | Qualifying (Must score 25%) |
| **Mains Paper B** | English Language Comprehension & Precis | 300 Marks | 3 Hours | Qualifying (Must score 25%) |
| **Mains Paper I** | Essay (2 Essays on philosophical or contemporary topics) | 250 Marks | 3 Hours | Counted for Final Merit Ranking |
| **Mains Paper II (GS I)** | Indian Heritage, History, Geography, Society | 250 Marks | 3 Hours | Counted for Final Merit Ranking |
| **Mains Paper III (GS II)**| Governance, Constitution, Polity, Social Justice, IR | 250 Marks | 3 Hours | Counted for Final Merit Ranking |
| **Mains Paper IV (GS III)**| Economy, Agriculture, Science & Tech, Environment, Security | 250 Marks | 3 Hours | Counted for Final Merit Ranking |
| **Mains Paper V (GS IV)** | Ethics, Integrity and Aptitude (Case Studies) | 250 Marks | 3 Hours | Counted for Final Merit Ranking |
| **Mains Paper VI & VII** | Optional Subject (Paper 1 & Paper 2) | 500 Marks (250 each) | 3 Hours each | Counted for Final Merit Ranking |
| **Personality Test (Interview)** | Assessment of character, clarity of thought, leadership | 275 Marks | ~30-45 Mins | Counted for Final Merit Ranking |
| **Grand Total** | **Written Mains (1750) + Interview (275)** | **2025 Marks** | **--** | **Final Rank Allotment** |

## 4-Phase Preparation Strategy

| Preparation Phase | Recommended Action Plan for Aspirants |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1: NCERT Foundation (Months 1-3)** | Read Class 6-12 NCERTs for History, Geography, Polity, and Economy. Understand foundational concepts without making notes initially. Select your Optional Subject wisely based on interest and scoring trends. |
| **Phase 2: Standard Reference Books (Months 4-6)** | Study Laxmikanth (Polity), Ramesh Singh or Nitin Singhania (Economy), Spectrum (Modern History), and GC Leong (Geography). Read The Hindu or Indian Express daily and maintain topic-wise notes for GS. |
| **Phase 3: Mains Answer Writing & Optional (Months 7-9)** | Complete your Optional Subject syllabus by month 8. Solve at least 2 mains questions daily. Practice structuring answers using introduction, bullet points, flowcharts, and positive conclusions. |
| **Phase 4: Prelims Test Series & Revision (Months 10-12)** | Shift focus to Prelims 90 days before the exam. Solve 40-50 full-length Prelims mocks and thoroughly review wrong answers. Practice CSAT papers weekly to avoid unexpected cut-off surprises. |

Success in UPSC is fundamentally a game of consistency, discipline, and emotional stamina. Stay updated with current affairs, revise periodically, and treat every mock test as a stepping stone toward the final merit list.
